signals.ai_share_evidence: No direct generation markers in commits (2023 web-UI edits: 'Update chatgpt.py', 'Update README.md'); the README's TOC-without-content 'guide' reads like a pasted article outline, but authorship cannot be determined from the snapshot; counter-evidence: the code was revisited in 2024 ('Updated the Code').

evidence.excerpt: Metadata: Python, 2 stars, 1 fork, 6 commits by 1 contributor over 2 distinct days (created 2023-03-29, last pushed 2024-09-21), no CI, no tests, deps declared.
2023-03-29: two 'Initial commit' entries, 'Update README.md' x2, 'Update chatgpt.py'; 2024-09-21 'Updated the Code' — one return visit eighteen months later.
Root entries: README.md, chatgpt.py (753 bytes), config.py (79 bytes), main.py (630 bytes), requirements.txt (18 bytes) — a minimal but complete runnable bot layout.

'Building a ChatGPT Discord Bot: A Step-by-Step Guide' with a 13-item Table of Contents (Prerequisites ... Troubleshooting Common Issues, Conclusion), followed only by three 'Instructions to Use' steps: venv, 'Install the necessary libraries from requirements.txt', 'Run the main.py script'.

counter_evidence.excerpt: The actual bot code exists and is coherent for the purpose: main.py, chatgpt.py, config.py, requirements.txt — everything the run instructions need is present.
The three concrete usage steps are complete and reference real files ('requirements.txt', 'main.py'), so a reader can run the bot even though the tutorial sections are missing.
'Updated the Code' on 2024-09-21 shows the owner maintained the code well after publication.

strongest_counter_evidence: The runnable artifact matches the run instructions exactly (main.py, requirements.txt present), so the functional claim is honest.
A later 2024 code update shows minimal but real maintenance.
A tiny personal utility bot is simple content, which the fairness rules exclude from slop.
counter_evidence_review.review_notes: The one genuinely unbacked element is the '13-section step-by-step guide' framing: the TOC promises content that is absent from the README. Everything else (small working bot with install/run steps) checks out at the structural level.

evidence_conflicts: README advertises a 13-section step-by-step guide via its Table of Contents, but the 1.4KB README contains none of those sections — only the three usage steps exist.

notes: A minimal ChatGPT Discord bot (three small Python files plus requirements.txt) with complete run instructions, created in 2023 and touched once in 2024. The README frames itself as a full step-by-step guide with a 13-item TOC, but none of those sections exist — the guide claim is unbacked while the runnable-bot claim is backed by the file listing. Simple content, honest at the code level, oversold at the doc level.
